topic: Seven strange borders, from Friendship Park to India's Cooch Behar enclaves
hook: Your map once had a field of Indian land inside Bangladeshi land inside Indian land inside Bangladesh, and it was completely real.
title: 7 Real Borders That Look Fake, Ending in India
description:
Seven real borders that look fake on a map, from a fence that runs into the Pacific at Friendship Park to a field inside a field inside a field in India. Every place here is real and you can look it up on your phone. Watch to the end for the strangest border of all.

#borders #geography #facts

scenes.narration: Your map once had a field of Indian land inside Bangladeshi land inside Indian land inside Bangladesh, and it was completely real.
scenes.headline: A Field Inside A Field

scenes.narration: That is number one on today's list of seven borders that make no sense, and it sits right in India.
scenes.headline: Number One Is Indian

scenes.narration: But we start with a fence where families meet through mesh, and the border walks straight into the sea.
scenes.headline: A Fence Into The Sea

scenes.narration: Each stop gets stranger than the last, and by the end you will see why the final border is the craziest.
scenes.headline: Stranger Every Stop

scenes.narration: These are real places on real maps, so you can check every one of them on your phone while you watch.
scenes.headline: Check Them Yourself

scenes.narration: We count down from seven, and seven is strange enough. Let's start with a hug through a fence.
scenes.headline: Counting Down From Seven

scenes.narration: Seven: Friendship Park, where the United States meets Mexico beside the Pacific Ocean, near San Diego and Tijuana.
scenes.headline: Friendship Park

scenes.narration: Your hug at this fence is real, because families have stood on both sides and met through the mesh.
scenes.headline: Meeting Through Mesh

scenes.narration: The park was opened in 1971 by Pat Nixon, then the First Lady of the United States.
scenes.headline: Opened In 1971

scenes.narration: She said she hoped the fence would not be there much longer, and it is still here today.
scenes.headline: The Fence Stayed

scenes.narration: Years ago people could touch hands through the bars. Later a fine mesh replaced them, and now it mostly allows fingertips.
scenes.headline: Only Fingertips

scenes.narration: Families split by the border still come here, because it is one of the few places they can see each other.
scenes.headline: Families Still Come

scenes.narration: Access on the American side has been cut back and reopened again over the years, so the rules keep changing.
scenes.headline: Rules Keep Changing

scenes.narration: Now look at the end of the map. The fence does not stop at the beach, it walks into the sea.
scenes.headline: It Walks Into The Sea

scenes.narration: Metal posts stand in the waves, so even the ocean has a border line you can see from the sand.
scenes.headline: A Border In The Waves

scenes.narration: A border you can touch with one fingertip is odd, but it is the mildest one on this list.
scenes.headline: The Mildest One

scenes.narration: Next, an American town that you can only reach by road if you drive through another country.
scenes.headline: Next: A Town Cut Off

scenes.narration: Six: Point Roberts, Washington, an American town that hangs off the bottom of Canada.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: The Canada-US border follows the forty-ninth parallel, and this little peninsula sits just south of that line.
scenes.headline: South Of The Line

scenes.narration: So it is America, but the only land road to it from the rest of the United States goes through Canada.
scenes.headline: Only Road Is Canadian

scenes.narration: Residents drive north into Canada, pass a border post, cross Canadian land, then pass another post to reach mainland America.
scenes.headline: Two Border Posts

scenes.narration: That means two border checks to travel between two American places, and a boat or plane is the only way around.
scenes.headline: Boat Or Plane

scenes.narration: When the border closed during the pandemic, the town was left in a very strange spot, and many people felt cut off.
scenes.headline: Cut Off In 2020

scenes.narration: Many Canadians own homes there, and students are bused through Canada to reach their schools in the United States.
scenes.headline: School Bus Through Canada

scenes.narration: All because a line on a map followed a parallel of latitude and ignored a peninsula hanging below it.
scenes.headline: A Ruler Decided

scenes.narration: Remember this: lines drawn with a ruler on a map never care about the ground underneath.
scenes.headline: Rulers Ignore Land

scenes.narration: Next, a German town where people spend Swiss money, and Switzerland is on almost every side.
scenes.headline: Next: Swiss Money

scenes.narration: Five: Büsingen am Hochrhein, a German village that sits almost completely inside Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: Look at the map and you will see a tiny German island, surrounded by Swiss land, next to the city of Schaffhausen.
scenes.headline: A German Island

scenes.narration: Its cars carry licence plates that begin with the letters BÜS, so you can spot a vehicle from this village on Swiss streets.
scenes.headline: Plates Start With BÜS

scenes.narration: The village is part of Germany, but it sits inside the Swiss customs area, so shops there follow Swiss rules.
scenes.headline: Swiss Customs Area

scenes.narration: Many people there use Swiss francs for daily shopping, even though they live in Germany and Germany uses the euro.
scenes.headline: Francs In Germany

scenes.narration: A few steps along the road and you pass from Germany into Switzerland without a guard or a gate.
scenes.headline: No Guard, No Gate

scenes.narration: Why does it exist? Old agreements and centuries of deals left this village German, and nobody ever changed it.
scenes.headline: Old Deals Stuck

scenes.narration: Locals live with two countries in one routine: a German address, Swiss money, and a Swiss town almost everywhere you look.
scenes.headline: Two Countries, One Routine

scenes.narration: If you thought that was odd, wait until you hear about a town that is Spanish but sits inside France.
scenes.headline: A Spanish Town In France

scenes.narration: That is next, and a special road keeps it connected to Spain.
scenes.headline: A Special Road

scenes.narration: Four: Llívia, a Spanish town sitting inside France, with French land on every side.
scenes.headline: Llívia

scenes.narration: In 1659 Spain and France signed the Treaty of the Pyrenees, and Spain handed over a set of villages.
scenes.headline: Treaty Of 1659

scenes.narration: But Llívia was counted as a town, not a village, so it stayed Spanish while the villages around it became French.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: That tiny word in a treaty is the reason a Spanish town now sits in the middle of French land.
scenes.headline: One Word Decided It

scenes.narration: A narrow road links it to the rest of Spain, and that road is called the neutral road.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: The road crosses French land, yet it is kept open so people can travel between the two Spanish places.
scenes.headline: Spain Through France

scenes.narration: Llívia even has a pharmacy said to be among the oldest in Europe, which visitors can see today.
scenes.headline: An Ancient Pharmacy

scenes.narration: Think about that: a word in a treaty from the sixteen hundreds still decides which flag flies over a town today.
scenes.headline: A Treaty Still Rules

scenes.narration: If you like strange places like this, subscribe, because tomorrow's video will be just as strange.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: Three is where the border goes missing completely, and it happens in the middle of a lake.
scenes.headline: The Missing Border

scenes.narration: Tourists swim and sail there every summer, yet three countries have never agreed where their line runs.
scenes.headline: Sailing Without A Line

scenes.narration: Three: Lake Constance, where Germany, Austria and Switzerland meet, and where the border is simply not agreed.
scenes.headline: Lake Constance

scenes.narration: On land, borders have posts and fences. On this lake, there is no officially agreed line in the water.
scenes.headline: No Line In The Water

scenes.narration: The three countries have different ideas about it, and no treaty has ever settled the matter for the whole lake.
scenes.headline: Never Agreed

scenes.narration: Experts talk about three ideas: a line down the middle, shared ownership of the whole lake, or each country owning its shore.
scenes.headline: Three Ideas, No Answer

scenes.narration: In practice, boats, ferries and fishing all work on local agreements, so daily life carries on.
scenes.headline: Ferries Keep Running

scenes.narration: So you can sail from one country to another on this lake, and no map can tell you the exact moment you crossed.
scenes.headline: When Did You Cross?

scenes.narration: A border that exists on land and disappears in the water is strange, but the next one is a whole country.
scenes.headline: Next: A Whole Country

scenes.narration: A country that fits entirely inside another country, with no sea and no neighbour except one.
scenes.headline: A Country Inside One

scenes.narration: That is not a riddle. Open your map and you can find it in southern Africa.
scenes.headline: Find It On Your Map

scenes.narration: It is number two, and then we come back home to India for the strangest of all.
scenes.headline: Then Back To India

scenes.narration: Two: Lesotho, an entire country that is completely surrounded by South Africa.
scenes.headline: Lesotho

scenes.narration: Every border Lesotho has is with one neighbour, so to travel anywhere abroad you must pass through South Africa first.
scenes.headline: One Neighbour Only

scenes.narration: Most countries have several neighbours. Lesotho has exactly one, and that border wraps all the way around it.
scenes.headline: Wrapped All Around

scenes.narration: It is also a mountain kingdom, with a king, a flag, its own currency and its own passport stamps.
scenes.headline: A Real Kingdom

scenes.narration: The country is often called the Kingdom in the Sky, because of its high mountains.
scenes.headline: Kingdom In The Sky

scenes.narration: Only a few countries in the world are fully surrounded like this, and the others are tiny European states.
scenes.headline: Very Few Like This

scenes.narration: So a whole country with its own king sits in the middle of another country's map, like a hole in a doughnut.
scenes.headline: A Hole In A Doughnut

scenes.narration: That is strange, but those borders at least kept one shape. The last one had a shape inside a shape inside a shape.
scenes.headline: Shape Inside A Shape

scenes.narration: And it was in India, along the Bangladesh border, in a place called Cooch Behar.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar, India

scenes.narration: One: the enclaves of Cooch Behar, India's strangest border, where villages of one country sat inside villages of another.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest Border

scenes.narration: For decades, over a hundred Indian pieces of land lay inside Bangladesh, and dozens of Bangladeshi pieces lay inside India.
scenes.headline: Pockets Of Each Country

scenes.narration: People in these pockets were often cut off from schools, markets and hospitals run by their own country.
scenes.headline: Cut Off From Home

scenes.narration: Then there was Dahala Khagrabari, a small farm plot, and its layers are why this one ends the list.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: It was Indian land inside a Bangladeshi plot, inside an Indian plot, inside Bangladesh. Four layers on one piece of ground.
scenes.headline: Four Layers Deep

scenes.narration: It was the world's only third-order enclave, and it was farmland that nobody lived on.
scenes.headline: The World's Only One

scenes.narration: In 2015 India and Bangladesh finally swapped these pockets, and the Dahala plot passed to Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: The 2015 Swap

scenes.narration: So the strangest border on this list is one you can no longer see on today's map, because it was finally fixed.
scenes.headline: Fixed, And Gone

scenes.narration: So we end where we began: a field inside a field inside a field, plus a fence running into the sea.
scenes.headline: Back To The Start

scenes.narration: Next video: more places that look fake on a map, but are real. See you there.
scenes.headline: Next: More Fake-Looking Places
